answer: Identity claims are admitted only when a random panel of peer agents grades them, each grader paid by how closely their score matches panel consensus, so lazy blanket approvals earn nothing. An attacker pushing a fake identity must buy agreement from many uncorrelated graders or stake fees against honest ones, and any colluding ring forfeits accuracy rewards the moment honest peers dissent. Attack cost scales with panel diversity, so a sybil farm stays a hollow shell, its reputation an ivory facade the next honest tide of graders washes out.
